targets.//: outputs covers dist/ only, even though this target also syncs engine.js into the Xcode wrapper's 'Shared (App)/Resources/' (scripts/sync-engine.mts). Same reason apps/safari-host-app/project.json leaves its sync undeclared, and it is a hard limitation rather than a choice: Nx's native glob reads the literal parens in 'Shared (App)' as group syntax and matches nothing, and neither backslash escapes nor [(] character classes fix it. dist/engine.js is therefore what a cache hit must restore, since the sync copies from there. This target is LOAD-BEARING for the shipped app: the native Detector tab gets its verdict from the engine, so a build that skips it ships a tab that cannot answer. Both Safari build paths invoke it (apps/extension/scripts/build-safari-app.mts and scripts/prepare-safari-build.sh), and project.pbxproj carries the engine.js reference. A bare `xcodebuild` does NOT — it copies whatever is already in Resources, which is how a stale bundle reaches a running app.
